title: Median
description:
Write `double median(std::vector<int> values)`: the middle value once the numbers are sorted. With an even count, it is the average of the two middle values. The vector is never empty.

The parameter is taken **by value** on purpose: you get your own copy, so `std::sort` can rearrange it without disturbing the caller.
hints: Sort with `std::sort(values.begin(), values.end());` (you own the copy, so changing it is fine). The middle index is `values.size() / 2`.
With an odd count, the median is `values[middle]`. With an even count, it is the average of `values[middle - 1]` and `values[middle]`, divided by `2.0` so you keep the half.
